title: Birth of Abraham
description: The year depends on whether Abram was born when Terah was 70 (Gen 11:26 read as birth order) or 130 (Gen 11:32 + 12:4 + Acts 7:4, Terah dying at 205 when Abram was 75). Ussher, Jones and CFAH-1 Table 1 take 130.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 2: CFAH-1 Table 1 (Ussher-Jones baseline): 1996 BC (Birth of Abraham) (no higher-tier year available).

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 1: Problem, Data, and Methodology," ARJ 15 (2022): 377–390, section "Our Assumptions (Declared Biases)", Table 1 "Biblically derived dates from Ussher and Jones"
chronologies.note: CFAH-1 Table 1 (Ussher-Jones biblical baseline adopted by CFAH); not a triangulated anchor point. Discussed in Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 6: The Old and Middle Kingdoms of Egypt," ARJ 18 (2025): 13–60, Argument 4 §2 "Terah's Famine and Abraham's Birth" ("In Ussher's chronology Abraham was born in 1996 BC (Ussher 2003, §64)").

chronologies.citation: Jones, Chronology of the Old Testament (15th ed., 2002), p. 77, Chart Four §A note (c) ("born BC 1996"); "Chronological Compendium", p. 1 ("Abraham born when Terah was 130 ... 2008")

chronologies.date: Terah "lived seventy years, and begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran"; Abram 75 when he left Haran after Terah died at 205

chronologies.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Second Age §63 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)
chronologies.note: CFAH-6 cites this as "Ussher 2003, §64"; the free transcription numbers it §63, so § numbering differs at least here.

chronologies.date: Birth of Abram: Anno Mundi 2008; 1922 B.C. (SBC)
chronologies.citation: Jordan, "Egypt in Biblical History," Biblical Chronology 5:8 (December 1993), chart "Anno Mundi / B.C. (SBC) / B.C. (CCC)" at the start of the article
chronologies.note: AM 2008 from Gen 11:26 with Acts 7:4 (Abram born when Terah was 130): BC 2:6 "The Abraham Connection" and BC 4:8 §2. B.C. year is Jordan's "SBC" (strictest Biblical chronology), which takes Daniel's 70 weeks literally from Cyrus (456 B.C. instead of the conventional 536 B.C.); not comparable one-to-one with Ussher/CFAH B.C. years. Same chart gives CCC "1952 or 2167".

chronologies.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 2, chart "Genesis 11:10 – 12 Genealogy"
chronologies.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 2008.

chronologies.date: AM 1948 if Terah was 70 (Gen 11:26 literal); AM 2008 if 130 (Gen 11:32 + 12:4)
chronologies.note: Straight arithmetic gives 1948; Ussher/Jones/CFAH/Raleigh reject it in favour of Terah aged 130 (AM 2008).

chronologies.date: "born in the two hundred and ninety-second year after the deluge; for Terah begat Abram in his seventieth year"
"from the Deludge untill Abrahams tyme" 292 years
chronologies.citation: Annals of Clonmacnoise (trans. Mageoghagan 1627, ed. Murphy 1896), prefatory "Memorandum" table of the ages of the world (between the p. 8 and p. 11 running heads; OCR)
chronologies.note: "Abrahams tyme" is not explicitly his birth. The Memorandum lists intervals 1656, 0292, 0500, 0480, 0410, 0432, 0134 against seven rows; the row/number pairing is read from OCR column order and should be checked against the page scan.

chronologies.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 782b
chronologies.note: Year cell "2691 2009 352". The third printed figure 352 is the column "Floud", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 175 at the end of the name is the lifespan he prints. The same section (Book II, ch. I, §VIII, sig. 164a) also prints "An. mundi 2008 dil. 352. natus Abraham, Eus. Aug. de Ciuit. Dei", introduced with "I conclude" and naming Eusebius and Augustine. The narrative sentence and the chronological table both print 2009. The 2008 is not given a second year. His table also prints the death at World 2183. 2009 + 175 is not 2183. Both figures are left as printed.

chronologies.date: which happened in the yeere of the World, 2009.
chronologies.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Book II, ch. I, §VIII, sig. 164a
chronologies.note: Narrative sentence. The chronological table prints the same yeere of the World. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. No BC conversion.

chronologies.date: by the Hebrew chronology, that Abraham was born A. M. 2008
chronologies.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 169 (facsimile PDF p. 265)
chronologies.note: He says this will appear hereafter very clearly. Page 251 prints A. M. 2001 for the same birth. Both are entered. See open question K3.

chronologies.date: Abram was born in the one hundred and thirtieth year of Terah, three hundred and fifty-two years after the Flood, A. M. 2001
chronologies.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book V, p. 251 (facsimile PDF p. 347)
chronologies.note: Page 252 says he has fixed this birth by the Hebrew chronology. The same paragraph also says three hundred and fifty-two years after the Flood. Page 169 prints A. M. 2008. Not reconciled. The Tolle Lege facsimile prints a clear 1 in A. M. 2001. On Internet Archive leaf n344 the same sentence is present, and the last digit is blotted, so that leaf alone does not confirm 1 or 8. The year stored is the clear facsimile digit. See open question K3.

chronologies.citation: Hales, A New Analysis of Chronology and Geography, History and Prophecy, 2nd ed., corrected and improved (London: C. J. G. & F. Rivington, 1830), vol. II, Synopsis of the Chronology, p. xxxiii
chronologies.note: Our check: 3155 minus 2153 is the printed 1002. That product is not stored.

chronologies.citation: Hales, A New Analysis of Chronology and Geography, History and Prophecy, 2nd ed., corrected and improved (London: C. J. G. & F. Rivington, 1830), vol. I, Table XI, Remarkable Eras, p. 101
